inspiral (EMRI) waveforms.

Builds come in CPU-only (`cpu_*`) and CUDA (`cuda12_*`, `cuda13_*`) flavours. On a machine with
an NVIDIA driver the CUDA flavour is selected automatically; use e.g.
`conda install fastemriwaveforms cuda-version=12` or `conda install "fastemriwaveforms=*=cpu*"`
to choose explicitly.

raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  name: FastEMRIWaveforms
  version: "2.2.1.post1"
  build: 0
  # CUDA major version of the current variant as a string ("12", "13"), or
  # "None" on CPU-only variants (and on platforms where conda-smithy emits no
  # cuda_compiler_version key at all, hence the `default`).
  cuda_major: ${{ cuda_compiler_version | default("None") | split(".") | first }}
  microarch_level: ${{ 1 if microarch_level is undefined else microarch_level | int }}
  # Build number layout: <cuda_major><microarch_level><build:02d>, e.g.
  #   cpu,    x86-64-v3, build 0 ->   300
  #   cuda12, x86-64,    build 0 -> 12100
  #   cuda13, x86-64,    build 0 -> 13100
  # For a given version the solver prefers the highest build number, so it picks
  # the newest CUDA build that the driver (__cuda) and any cuda-version pin
  # allow, and falls back to the best CPU build the machine supports.
  build_number: ${{ build + (microarch_level | int) * 100 + ((cuda_major | int) * 1000 if cuda_major != "None" else 0) }}
  microarch_option: ${{ ("-Ccmake.define.FEW_MARCH=x86-64-v" ~ microarch_level if (microarch_level | int) > 1 else "-Ccmake.define.FEW_MARCH=x86-64")  if (unix and x86_64) else "" }}

recipe:
  name: ${{ name|lower }}-split
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/BlackHolePerturbationToolkit/FastEMRIWaveforms/archive/refs/tags/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 803155d4b2a7e516b5479fca7bae967fdaf2393a7ef73a9c38457720d1032930

build:
  number: ${{ build_number }}
  skip:
    - match(python, "<3.12")
    # The CUDA backend is only shipped for linux-64 and linux-aarch64
    - cuda_major != "None" and (not linux or ppc64le)
    # CUDA builds also contain the CPU backend, but are only built for the
    # baseline microarch level to keep the CI matrix manageable
    - cuda_major != "None" and microarch_level > 1
    # FEW only provides backends for these CUDA major versions
    - cuda_major not in ("None", "12", "13")
    # TEMPORARY: cupy-core 14.2.0 constrains scipy <1.18, but only scipy 1.18
    # exists for Python 3.15, so cupy cannot be installed there. Python 3.15
    # gets cpu builds only until cupy-feedstock relaxes that constraint; then
    # remove this line, bump `build` and rerender.
    - cuda_major != "None" and match(python, ">=3.15")

outputs:
  - package:
      name: fastemriwaveforms
      version: ${{ version }}
    build:
      number: ${{ build_number }}
      # cpu_py312h<hash>_300, cuda12_py312h<hash>_12100, cuda13_py312h<hash>_13100
      # so that `fastemriwaveforms=*=cpu*` / `=*=cuda12*` select a flavour.
      string: ${{ ("cuda" ~ cuda_major if cuda_major != "None" else "cpu") }}_py${{ python | version_to_buildstring }}h${{ hash }}_${{ build_number }}
      script:
        env:
          SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION: ${{ version }}
        content:
          - if: cuda_major != "None"
            then: >-
              ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv
              -Ccmake.define.FEW_WITH_GPU=ON
              -Ccmake.define.FEW_CUDA_ARCH="${CUDAARCHS:-all-major}"
              ${{ microarch_option }}
            else: >-
              ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv
              -Ccmake.define.FEW_WITH_GPU=OFF
              ${{ microarch_option }}
      python:
        entry_points:
          - few_citations = few.cmd.citations:main
          - few_files = few.cmd.files:main
    requirements:
      build:
        - if: build_platform != target_platform
          then:
            - python
            - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
            - numpy
            - scikit-build-core
            - cython
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
        - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
        - if: cuda_major != "None"
          then:
            - ${{ compiler('cuda') }}
            - if: build_platform != target_platform
              then:
                - cuda-version ${{ cuda_compiler_version }}.*
                - cuda-driver-dev
                - cuda-cudart-dev
                - libcublas-dev
                - libcusparse-dev
        - ninja
        - cmake
        - make
        - if: unix and x86_64 and microarch_level < 4
          then: x86_64-microarch-level ${{ microarch_level }}.*
      host:
        - python
        - pip
        - scikit-build-core
        - setuptools_scm
        - cython
        - numpy
        - if: cuda_major != "None"
          then:
            - cuda-version ${{ cuda_compiler_version }}.*
            - cuda-driver-dev
            - cuda-cudart-dev
            - libcublas-dev
            - libcusparse-dev
      run:
        - python
        - h5py
        - jsonschema
        - lisaconstants
        - multispline
        - numba
        - numpy
        - nvidia-ml-py
        - platformdirs
        - pydantic
        - pyyaml
        - requests
        - rich
        - scipy
        - tqdm
        - wrapt
        - if: unix and x86_64 and microarch_level == 4
          then: _x86_64-microarch-level >=${{ microarch_level }}
        - if: cuda_major != "None"
          then:
            # Only installable on machines with an NVIDIA driver new enough for
            # this CUDA major; elsewhere the solver falls back to a cpu build.
            - __cuda >=${{ cuda_major }}
            - ${{ pin_compatible('cuda-version', lower_bound='x', upper_bound='x') }}
            # cupy 13.x caps numpy (<2.3) only in its pip metadata, so the
            # solver can pair it with a newer numpy and `pip check` fails
            - cupy >=14
            - cuda-cudart
            - libcublas
            - libcusparse
      ignore_run_exports:
        from_package:
          - if: cuda_major != "None"
            then:
              - ${{ compiler('cuda') }}
              - cuda-driver-dev
              - cuda-cudart-dev
              - libcublas-dev
              - libcusparse-dev
    tests:
      - if: microarch_level < 4
        then:
          - python:
              imports:
                - few
                - few.tests
                - few_backend_cpu
          - requirements:
              run:
                - pip
                - if: cuda_major != "None"
                  # libcuda stub, needed to load the CUDA backend without a GPU
                  then: cuda-driver-dev
            script:
              # set via `env` rather than `VAR=value cmd`, which cmd.exe on
              # Windows does not understand
              env:
                FEW_ENABLED_BACKENDS: cpu
              content:
                - pip check
                - python -c "import importlib.metadata; assert importlib.metadata.version('fastemriwaveforms') == '${{ version }}'"
                - python -c "import few; few.get_backend('cpu')"
                - if: cuda_major != "None"
                  then: python -c "import few_backend_cuda${{ cuda_major }}x.pyinterp"
                - python -m few.tests --disable testfile
    about:
      summary: Blazingly fast EMRI waveforms
      description: |
        This package contains the highly modular framework for fast and accurate extreme mass ratio
        inspiral (EMRI) waveforms.

        Builds come in CPU-only (`cpu_*`) and CUDA (`cuda12_*`, `cuda13_*`) flavours. On a machine with
        an NVIDIA driver the CUDA flavour is selected automatically; use e.g.
        `conda install fastemriwaveforms cuda-version=12` or `conda install "fastemriwaveforms=*=cpu*"`
        to choose explicitly.
      license: MIT
      license_file: LICENSE
      homepage: https://github.com/BlackHolePerturbationToolkit/FastEMRIWaveforms
      repository: https://github.com/BlackHolePerturbationToolkit/FastEMRIWaveforms
      documentation: https://fastemriwaveforms.readthedocs.io/en/v${{ version }}/

  # Transitional metapackage so that environments which installed the old
  # fastemriwaveforms-cuda12x plugin upgrade cleanly to the CUDA 12 build of
  # fastemriwaveforms. Drop this output after a release or two.
  - package:
      name: fastemriwaveforms-cuda12x
      version: ${{ version }}
    build:
      number: ${{ build_number }}
      skip: cuda_major != "12"
    requirements:
      run:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('fastemriwaveforms', exact=True) }}
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - few
          pip_check: false
    about:
      summary: Transitional package, use fastemriwaveforms instead
      description: |
        Deprecated: the CUDA 12 backend is now part of the `cuda12_*` builds of fastemriwaveforms.
        This package only exists to upgrade environments that installed the former plugin.
      license: MIT
      license_file: LICENSE
      homepage: https://github.com/BlackHolePerturbationToolkit/FastEMRIWaveforms

about:
  summary: Blazingly fast EMRI waveforms
  description: |
    This package contains the highly modular framework for fast and accurate extreme mass ratio

  license: MIT

  documentation: https://fastemriwaveforms.readthedocs.io/en/v${{ version }}/
